title: Zariski and small etale quasi-coherent modules agree functorially
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. The association $F\mapsto F_{\mathrm{et}}$, where $F_{\mathrm{et}}(u:U\to T)=\Gamma(U,u^*F)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], is an equivalence from quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] to quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The forward functor is tensor pullback by the canonical morphism of ringed sites $\epsilon:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, namely $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\epsilon^{-1}\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{Zar}}}\epsilon^{-1}(-)$. Its inverse is restriction to Zariski opens; in particular the unit and counit comparisons are the identity on sections of open subschemes. This equivalence identifies ordinary invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] with line modules on the small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every scheme morphism $a:U\to T$, it has a canonical natural comparison $(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq a_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_{\mathrm{et}}$, where the left pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback] and the right is tensor pullback between the ringed etale topoi. If $a$ is quasi-compact and separated [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], then for every quasi-coherent Zariski module $H$ on $U$ the two direct images are quasi-coherent and there is a canonical natural isomorphism $(a_*H)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq a_{\mathrm{et},*}(H_{\mathrm{et}})$ whose restriction to Zariski opens is the identity on sections.

proof.text: Write $L_T=\epsilon_T^*$ and $R_T=\epsilon_{T,*}$. By [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom], $L_TF$ is the specified tensor-sections sheaf, is site quasi-coherent, is fully faithful on quasi-coherent modules, and its unit is the identity on open sections. By [lem-trf-etale-presented-module-effective-recovery], every site quasi-coherent $G$ has quasi-coherent $R_TG$ and invertible counit, also the identity on open sections. Thus these restricted adjoint functors are inverse equivalences, with the stated normalization.

proof.text: The invertible-module assertion is [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison]: its functor $A_T(L)=L_{\mathrm{et}}$, with $A_T(h)_u=\Gamma(U,u^*h)$, is an equivalence from ordinary invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with all module maps, onto the modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ that become isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ on the localized sites of a jointly surjective etale family, which are exactly the line modules of [def-trf-algebraic-space] for the scheme $T$. An invertible module is quasi-coherent by definition, so [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] identifies $L_TL$ with $L_{\mathrm{et}}=A_T(L)$, and $L_Th$ with $A_T(h)$. Hence $L_T$ sends invertible modules to line modules, and every line module is isomorphic to some $L_TL$. Both classes are full subcategories, so the equivalence of step 1 restricts to the claimed equivalence between invertible modules and line modules.

source.place: 05VG, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties, finite locally free case (rank one), via the existing rank-one comparison node

proof.text: For arbitrary $a:U\to T$, [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] gives the canonical natural isomorphism $L_Ua^*F\simeq a_{\mathrm{et}}^*L_TF$. The module $a^*F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. The tensor-sections identifications of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] therefore turn this into $(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq a_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_{\mathrm{et}}$, as claimed.

source.place: 03FH(2) and 03LC(1): specialize the canonical module-functor comparison.

proof.text: For quasi-compact separated $a$ and quasi-coherent $H$, [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] gives quasi-coherent $a_*H$ and the canonical sectionwise isomorphism $L_T(a_*H)\simeq a_{\mathrm{et},*}L_UH$, natural in $H$ and equal to the identity on open sections. By [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] its source is site quasi-coherent. The isomorphic target is therefore site quasi-coherent as well. Replacing both $L$-images by their tensor-sections descriptions yields exactly the required direct-image isomorphism and normalization.
